result.topic_en: Series and infinite products evaluated in terms of a function Φ (related to inverse-tangent integrals), including log-sums with odd-integer weights and resulting infinite product identities.
result.transcription:
Add. Ms. a 94^{18 (66)} (66) (2)
(8) $\frac{\sin x}{1^2}(1-\frac{1}{\alpha})\cos x + \frac{\sin 2x}{2^2}(1-\frac{1}{\alpha})^2\cos^2 x + \cdots$
$+ \frac{\sin(x+\frac12\pi)}{1^2}(1-\alpha)\sin x + \frac{\sin 2(x+\frac12\pi)}{2^2}(1-\alpha)^2\sin^2 x + \cdots$
$= \Phi(\tan x) - \Phi(\alpha\tan x) + x\log\alpha$.
If $-1<x<1$, then
(9) $\log(1-\frac{x^2}{1^2}) - 3\log(1-\frac{x^2}{3^2}) + 5\log(1-\frac{x^2}{5^2}) - \cdots$
$= \frac{4}{\pi}\{\Phi(1) - \Phi(\tan\frac14\pi(1-x))\} + \log\tan\frac14\pi(1-x)$.
As an example we have
(10) $(1-\frac{4}{3^2})(1-\frac{4}{9^2})^{-3}(1-\frac{4}{15^2})^5(1-\frac{4}{21^2})^{-7}\cdots$
$= \frac{e^{\frac{4}{3\pi}\Phi(1)}}{(2+\sqrt3)^{2/3}}$.
If $x$ is real, then
(11) $\log(1+\frac{x^2}{1^2}) - 3\log(1+\frac{x^2}{3^2}) + 5\log(1+\frac{x^2}{5^2}) - \cdots$
$= \frac{4}{\pi}\{\Phi(1) - \Phi(e^{-\frac12\pi x})\} - 2x\tan^{-1}e^{-\frac12\pi x}$.
For example
(12) $(1+\{\frac{2}{\pi}\log(2+\sqrt3)\}^2)(1+\{\frac{2}{3\pi}\log(2+\sqrt3)\}^2)^{-3}(1+\{\frac{2}{5\pi}\log(2+\sqrt3)\}^2)^5\cdots$
$= e^{\frac{4}{3\pi}\Phi(1)}$
It follows from (9) and (11) that, if $-1<\beta<1$ and $\frac12\pi\alpha$
$= \log\tan\frac14\pi(1+\beta)$, then
(13) $\left(\frac{1^2+\alpha^2}{1^2-\beta^2}\right)\left(\frac{3^2-\beta^2}{3^2+\alpha^2}\right)^3\left(\frac{5^2+\alpha^2}{5^2-\beta^2}\right)^5\left(\frac{7^2-\beta^2}{7^2+\alpha^2}\right)^7\cdots\cdots$
$= e^{\frac12\pi\alpha\beta}$.
